title: Swap an orbital replacement unit
instruction: Pull the red unit out of the bay and stow it in the return slot, turned 90 degrees to fit, then seat the grey spare in the empty bay.
context: Replacing an orbital replacement unit is the core servicing operation on the ISS and on planned satellite-servicing missions: the bay must be empty before the spare goes in, and the removed unit must be stowed, not left loose. Unlike a single insertion, the bay has to be emptied first, the removed unit has to be re-keyed 90 degrees into a slot only the left arm reaches, and the spare starts where only the right arm reaches, so the two arms must hand the bay over in order. A 1 g tabletop analogue, not microgravity; gravity and keyed pockets with 5 mm clearance stand in for captive bolts, blind-mate connectors and grapple fixtures.
setup: On the table, x forward from the arm bases, y left, z up. Two loose units, each a 60 x 40 x 90 mm rigid block of 0.15 kg, matte: the red unit (sRGB 0.85, 0.12, 0.12) stands in the bay, 260 mm in front of the base line on the midline, 60 mm side along x; the grey spare (sRGB 0.70, 0.70, 0.72) stands on a white mark pad, 90 mm along x by 70 mm along y and 2 mm thick, centred 240 mm in front of the right arm's base and 15 mm outboard of it, turned 90 degrees (60 mm side along y). Two fixed pockets, dark grey (sRGB 0.25, 0.25, 0.27), with 40 mm tall and 10 mm thick walls on an open floor: the bay at the red unit's position, inner opening 70 mm along x by 50 mm along y (outer footprint 90 x 70 mm); the return slot 260 mm in front of the left arm's base and 5 mm inboard of it, inner opening 50 mm along x by 70 mm along y (outer footprint 70 x 90 mm), so a unit fits it only turned 90 degrees from the bay. Each pocket gives a unit 5 mm of clearance per side, and a unit turned 90 degrees from a pocket's key cannot enter it. The red unit's top stands 50 mm above the bay rim. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the objects' end state; a unit standing in its pocket counts whether or not a gripper still touches it. Upright: the unit's 90 mm axis within 5 degrees of vertical, either end down, bottom within 3 mm of the table, at rest (moving under 10 mm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s). Seated: upright, centred within 7.5 mm of the pocket and keyed within 11 degrees of its long axis, which any unit standing flat inside a pocket meets (at most 7.1 mm and 10.3 degrees off). 0 while the red unit is still in the bay (its centre within 50 mm of the bay centre, at any height, including on top of the spare), whatever the spare does. Red unit out and lying, tilted or on a wall: 0. Red unit out and upright on the table, not seated in the slot, spare not seated: 0.25. Red unit seated in the return slot, spare not seated in the bay: 0.5. Spare seated in the bay with the red unit out but not upright: 0.5. Spare seated in the bay with the red unit upright but not seated in the slot: 0.75. Spare seated in the bay and red unit seated in the return slot: 1.0. A spare placed anywhere but the bay earns nothing. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. On the real rig a pocket or the pad moved more than 5 mm ends the trial at 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the red unit back in the bay with its 60 mm side along x and the grey unit on the pad with its 60 mm side along y.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours; the pockets and pad are massless fixtures that cannot move. A real unit is retained by captive fasteners and blind-mate connectors and handled by a grapple fixture; here gravity and 5 mm of clearance hold it, with no latch, connector or fastener modelled. Earth gravity, not microgravity.
